question: Has road safety for pedestrians in Brooklyn gotten better since 2013? Make a chart suitable for a local news story and summarize the findings.

options.metric: Annual reported pedestrian casualties, the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured and number_of_pedestrians_killed across Brooklyn crashes
options.denominator: None; a count, not adjusted for population, pedestrian trips, or miles walked
options.reason: Combining injuries and deaths summarizes the annual reported burden of pedestrian harm in one legible series.
options.answer: This file cannot establish whether pedestrian road safety improved; it records 3,671 reported Brooklyn pedestrian casualties in 2013, a low of 1,798 in 2020, and 2,874 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This file can answer only part of whether Brooklyn pedestrian road safety improved: the chart counts reported pedestrian injuries plus deaths in Brooklyn crashes for each calendar year from 2013 through 2025, and records span January 1 through December 31 in every included year. The count was 3,671 in 2013, reached a low of 1,798 in 2020, and was 2,874 in 2025. This is a defensible direct measure of reported harm burden, but without pedestrian trips or another exposure denominator it cannot establish whether pedestrians became safer. Of 2,132,218 dated crash rows in 2013-2025, 659,713 (30.9%) lacked a usable borough and were excluded; all 473,801 included Brooklyn rows had nonmissing injury and death fields, and 2026 was excluded because it is partial (9,700 Brooklyn crashes through June 11).

options.metric: Annual reported pedestrian deaths, the sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed across Brooklyn crashes
options.denominator: None; a count, not adjusted for population, pedestrian trips, or miles walked
options.reason: Deaths are the most severe pedestrian crash outcome and merit a focused series separate from injuries.
options.answer: This file cannot establish whether pedestrian road safety improved; it records 30 pedestrian deaths in Brooklyn crashes in 2013, a low of 17 in 2020, and 39 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This file can answer only part of whether Brooklyn pedestrian road safety improved: the chart counts reported pedestrian deaths in Brooklyn crashes for each calendar year from 2013 through 2025, and records span January 1 through December 31 in every included year. The count was 30 in 2013, reached a low of 17 in 2020, and was 39 in 2025. A fatality-only count highlights the most severe outcome, but without pedestrian trips or another exposure denominator it cannot establish whether pedestrians became safer. Of 2,132,218 dated crash rows in 2013-2025, 659,713 (30.9%) lacked a usable borough and were excluded; none of the 473,801 included Brooklyn crash rows had a missing pedestrian-death field, and 2026 was excluded because it is partial (9,700 Brooklyn crashes through June 11).

answer:
1. This file cannot establish whether pedestrian road safety improved; reported pedestrian injuries plus deaths in Brooklyn crashes numbered 3,671 in 2013, reached a low of 1,798 in 2020, and numbered 2,874 in 2025 ([casualty chart](./out/option_1.png)).
2. This file cannot establish whether pedestrian road safety improved; Brooklyn crashes recorded 30 pedestrian deaths in 2013, a low of 17 in 2020, and 39 in 2025 ([fatality chart](./out/option_2.png)).
